# PRD: Team Workspaces

**Author:** [name]
**Status:** Draft
**Last updated:** 2026-10-06

> I don't have details about your product, so this PRD is written for a generic SaaS app where users currently own their data individually. Bracketed items `[like this]` are placeholders or assumptions to confirm.

---

## 1. Summary

Today, every resource in the product belongs to a single user account. This PRD proposes **Team Workspaces**: shared containers where multiple users collaborate on resources under common ownership, permissions, and billing.

## 2. Problem Statement

- Users who work in groups share logins or export and import data by hand, which is insecure and error-prone.
- There is no way to onboard or offboard a collaborator without transferring individual accounts.
- Organizations can't buy for a group, which blocks larger deals and caps expansion revenue.
- Users report the lack of collaboration as a top reason for churn or for choosing competitors. `[cite support/sales data]`

## 3. Goals

1. Let users create a workspace and invite teammates to collaborate on shared resources.
2. Provide role-based access control that admins can understand and trust.
3. Support workspace-level billing and seat management.
4. Migrate existing individual users without data loss or disruption.

## 4. Non-Goals (v1)

- SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning (planned for v2, Enterprise)
- Nested teams or sub-workspaces
- Cross-workspace resource sharing
- Custom roles
- Real-time presence or co-editing, unless it already exists in the product

## 5. Target Users and Personas

| Persona | Needs |
|---|---|
| **Workspace Owner** | Controls billing, membership, and deletion |
| **Admin** | Manages members and settings |
| **Member** | Creates and edits shared resources |
| **Viewer / Guest** | Read-only access, often external |
| **Existing solo user** | Wants to keep working as before and optionally upgrade to a team |

## 6. User Stories

- As a user, I can create a workspace with a name and slug.
- As an admin, I can invite people by email and assign them a role.
- As an invitee, I can accept an invite whether or not I already have an account.
- As a member, I can switch between my personal space and any workspaces I belong to.
- As a member, I can create resources inside a workspace that every member can see, subject to role.
- As an owner, I can transfer ownership, remove members, and delete the workspace.
- As an owner, I can manage seats and billing for the workspace.
- As an admin, I can view an audit log of membership and permission changes.

## 7. Functional Requirements

### 7.1 Workspace Management
- **FR-1:** Any authenticated user can create a workspace. Creator becomes Owner.
- **FR-2:** Workspace has name, slug (unique, URL-safe), avatar, and created date.
- **FR-3:** Owners can rename, transfer ownership, and delete the workspace. Deletion requires confirmation and has a 30-day soft-delete window.
- **FR-4:** A user can belong to multiple workspaces. `[Limit?]`

### 7.2 Membership and Invitations
- **FR-5:** Admins and Owners can invite by email, singly or in bulk.
- **FR-6:** Invites expire after 7 days, can be revoked, and can be resent.
- **FR-7:** Invitees without an account are guided through sign-up, then land in the workspace.
- **FR-8:** Optional domain-based auto-join, controlled by an admin. `[v1.1]`
- **FR-9:** Members can leave a workspace. The last Owner cannot leave without transferring ownership.

### 7.3 Roles and Permissions

| Capability | Owner | Admin | Member | Viewer |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Delete workspace / transfer ownership | ✅ | | | |
| Manage billing | ✅ | | | |
| Invite / remove members | ✅ | ✅ | | |
| Change roles (except Owner) | ✅ | ✅ | | |
| Create / edit / delete resources | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | |
| View resources | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| View audit log | ✅ | ✅ | | |

- **FR-10:** Every API endpoint and query enforces workspace scoping and role checks server-side.
- **FR-11:** Permission changes take effect immediately, including for active sessions.

### 7.4 Resource Ownership
- **FR-12:** Every resource belongs to exactly one owner context: a personal space or a workspace.
- **FR-13:** Users can move their personal resources into a workspace they belong to. Moves are one-way unless an admin approves.
- **FR-14:** When a member is removed, resources they created remain in the workspace.

### 7.5 Navigation and UX
- **FR-15:** A workspace switcher is always visible in the primary navigation.
- **FR-16:** The active workspace is reflected in the URL (`/w/{slug}/...`) so links are shareable.
- **FR-17:** Settings pages: General, Members, Billing, Audit Log.

### 7.6 Billing
- **FR-18:** Workspaces are billed per seat. `[or flat tier, confirm pricing model]`
- **FR-19:** Adding or removing members adjusts seats with proration.
- **FR-20:** Failed payment triggers a grace period, then read-only mode. Data is never deleted for non-payment inside the grace window.

### 7.7 Notifications
- **FR-21:** Emails for invitation, role change, removal, ownership transfer, and billing events.
- **FR-22:** In-app notifications for invites and mentions `[if applicable]`.

### 7.8 Audit Log
- **FR-23:** Record who did what and when for membership, role, billing, and deletion events. Retain 90 days in v1.

## 8. Non-Functional Requirements

- **Security:** Strict tenant isolation, with workspace ID enforced at the data layer (e.g., row-level security or mandatory query scoping). Pen test before GA.
- **Performance:** Workspace switch under 500 ms p95. Permission checks add under 20 ms p95.
- **Scalability:** Support workspaces of up to `[1,000]` members in v1.
- **Reliability:** Invite and billing flows are idempotent and safe to retry.
- **Privacy/Compliance:** Honor GDPR deletion and export at both user and workspace level. Document the data processor/controller split.
- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.1 AA for all new UI.
- **Observability:** Metrics and alerts on invite failures, permission-denied spikes, and billing sync errors.

## 9. Migration Plan

1. Add a nullable `workspace_id` to shareable resources, with backfill tooling.
2. Existing users keep a **Personal Space** and nothing changes by default.
3. Offer a guided "Create a team from your account" flow that moves selected resources.
4. Ship behind a feature flag. Roll out to internal users, then a 5% cohort, then 25%, 50%, and GA.
5. Provide a rollback path through flag-off, with no destructive schema changes until stable.

## 10. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target `[baseline TBD]` |
|---|---|
| % of active accounts in ≥1 workspace with 2+ members | 20% within 6 months |
| Invite acceptance rate | ≥ 60% |
| Median time from workspace creation to 2nd member joining | < 24 hours |
| Workspace-plan conversion / ARPA lift | `[+X%]` |
| Churn of workspace accounts vs. solo accounts | ≥ 20% lower |
| Permission-related support tickets | < 2% of workspace accounts/month |

**Guardrails:** no regression in solo-user activation, page load times, or error rates.

## 11. Rollout and Milestones

| Phase | Scope | Target |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | Design, data model, security review | Weeks 1–3 |
| M1 | Workspace CRUD, membership, roles, scoping (internal alpha) | Weeks 4–9 |
| M2 | Invitations, switcher UX, resource moves, audit log (beta) | Weeks 10–14 |
| M3 | Billing and seats, migration tooling, hardening | Weeks 15–18 |
| GA | Staged rollout and docs | Week 19+ |

## 12. Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-tenant data leakage | Critical | Data-layer enforcement, automated isolation tests, pen test |
| Complex migration of existing data | High | Non-destructive approach, dry-run tooling, feature flag |
| Permission model too rigid | Medium | Ship 4 roles now, design schema to allow custom roles later |
| Billing edge cases (proration, seat disputes) | Medium | Use billing provider's native seat features, thorough test matrix |
| Confusing personal vs. workspace context | Medium | Clear switcher, persistent context indicator, usability testing |

## 13. Open Questions

1. What is the pricing model: per-seat, flat tiers, or free up to N members?
2. Do guests/external collaborators count as paid seats?
3. Should one user be able to own multiple workspaces, and is there a cap?
4. Can personal resources be moved back out of a workspace?
5. What is the retention policy for deleted workspaces beyond 30 days?
6. Which existing features (API keys, integrations, webhooks) need to become workspace-scoped?
7. Is SSO required for any committed customers, which would pull it into v1?

## 14. Dependencies

- Auth/session layer changes to carry active workspace context
- Billing provider integration updates
- Transactional email templates
- Design: switcher, settings, and invite flows
- Legal/security review of the data-processing terms

---

If you'd like, I can tailor this to your actual product (tell me the domain and stack), trim it to a one-pager, or save it as a Markdown file in your project.
